request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the
as-of date, or nothing). While it is set, every figure and flag on the screen for the signed-in
user, in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates and the summary, is shown as
it stood at the end of the last day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's
today was on or before the as-of date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date
stands in for the sheet's today in every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals,
retirements, the grade and rate in force). The audit file is unaffected, and every change,
a statement as of a date included, is refused with its usual error while the as-of date is set.
The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen; other users are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the
as-of date, or nothing). While it is set, every figure and flag on the screen for the signed-in
user, in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates and the summary, is shown as
it stood at the end of the last day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's
today was on or before the as-of date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date
stands in for the sheet's today in every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals,
retirements, the grade and rate in force). The audit file is unaffected, and every change,
a statement as of a date included, is refused with its usual error while the as-of date is set.
The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen; other users are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The as-of view is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:** the figures on screen are worked out in the browser from what the server returns. So rather than change any of those calculations, I made the server able to return the sheet as it stood at the end of a given day.

- **Screen controls** (`features/sheet/asof.slot.tsx`): the date entry `asof-date`, the buttons `asof-set` and `asof-clear`, and `sheet-asof`, which shows the date or nothing. The date is kept in the address bar (`?asOf=`), so it belongs to that user's screen only and other users are unaffected. Setting or clearing it reloads all of the sheet's data.
- **Reading** (`api/http.ts`): while the date is set, every request for data carries it, and the server's read endpoints (sheet, people, claims, rates, settings, periods) answer as of that day. They use the history logs the app already kept for statements taken "as of" a date.
- **The date stands in for today**: on screen, all figures (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force) use the as-of date. The server does the same for the grade it reports, whether a claim is deferred, and the settings in force. The `sheet-today` display still shows the real today.
- **Changes are refused**: every change sent while the date is set is marked as such. The server's existing filter that blocks viewers and archived sheets now rejects these too, before anything is written or audited. Each form shows its usual error.
- **New history** (migration `V48__as_of_view.sql`): the logs didn't yet cover a few things, so I added:
  - the day a sheet was archived;
  - the day each statement was taken. A cancelled statement is now marked cancelled with the day, instead of being deleted, so earlier days can still show it.
  - the day each period was added, and a history of each close, soft-close and reopen with the totals fixed at the time.

**Two behaviours you should know about:**
- **Some settings are not dated:** the policy date, permissions, grace days and period numbering always show their current values, even in the as-of view. This matches how statements taken as of a date already work, but strictly the request asks for every change to be dated.
- **Fix to the statement date entry:** a refused "statement as of a date" used to leave its date in the entry, so the next plain Statement click silently sent that date again and was refused too. The test hit this in scenario 2. The entry now clears after every attempt, whether it worked or not.
